column3: The Hebrew says the Gibeonites were in their midst, rather than living near them.
The Hebrew uses “they were afraid” without explicitly naming Adoni-zedek and his people.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says to come up to me and treats Gibeon as singular.
The Hebrew repeats king with each city and names the Amorite collectively in the singular.
The Hebrew retains the image of not letting the hands slacken from the servants and explicitly says to come up.
The Hebrew says Joshua went up from Gilgal and joins the mighty men with “and”.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly describes going up from Gilgal.
The Hebrew continues with singular verbs for striking and pursuing, without explicitly identifying Israel as a new subject.
The Hebrew first calls them large stones, later hailstones, and uses singular sword for what the Israelites killed with.
The Hebrew names the Amorite collectively in the singular and retains the eyes of Israel.
The Hebrew says the sun did not hurry to go down, rather than explicitly saying it delayed.
Close to the Hebrew.

The Hebrew narrates their fleeing and hiding without a distinct pluperfect construction.
Close to the Hebrew.

The Hebrew describes finishing a very great striking and says the surviving remainder entered the fortified cities.
The Hebrew calls the returning force all the people and retains the image of sharpening the tongue against the Israelites.
The Hebrew explicitly repeats “from the cave.”
The Hebrew separately says they did so and repeats the king title for each city.
The Hebrew repeats Joshua’s name and uses pronouns rather than repeating commanders when they approach.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says he hung them and that they were hanging; it does not separately add their bodies or make leaving them another action.
The Hebrew makes their taking down, throwing, and placing stones active plural actions.
The Hebrew retains the mouth of the sword and calls each person a soul.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses pronouns rather than repeating Joshua or naming Libnah’s king again and retains the mouth of the sword and each soul.
